newsitem.title: UK: U.K. air cargo forum holds inaugural meeting.
newsitem.headline: U.K. air cargo forum holds inaugural meeting.

text.p: The British air cargo industry has set up a forum made up of some 20 representatives of major airlines, air freight forwarders and shippers to have a common meeting ground where they can discuss mutual problems.
The meeting of the U.K. Air Freight Forum included officials from the Freight Transport Association's (FTA) British Shippers Council and from the British International Freight Association (BIFA).

If the air cargo industry is going to succeed in improving its product, it is essential that all sides of the industry sit down and talk to each other and agree what they are trying to do, Mike Goodyear of Royal Mail International and chairman of the FTA's Air Transport Committee told a press conference.

Intergrators were not present at Tuesday's session, but Goodyear said this was not a deliberate exclusion. A forum statement said keeping it to a manageable size is seen as crucial if it is to achieve results and not become a mere talking shop.
Goodyear and other forum members said this was the first time the three sides of the industry had listened to each other's points of viewe rather than just arguing their cases.
As a result even one session of positive discussion had revealed misconceptions on what constituted a good service.

Forum members said they wanted to avoid public posturing of known positions as took place at the recent industry conference in Dubai. Instead they wanted to establish a dialogue between the different sectors of the industry with the object of benefitting the actual user of air freight.
Shippers wanted goods delivered on time but airlines might believe they were fulfilling their task if went as booked.
A sub-group of the forum will meet within the next couple of months to try and reach consensus on what is meant by quality and efficiency standards.
"We need to have common standards we can measure performance against - not a long list but say half a dozen,"one forum member told the press conference.
"But standards do exist and the emphasis is on finding consensus on definition rather than setting rules," another said.

The sub-group which will represent all sections of the industry will report back to the full forum at its next meeting in the first or second week in February 1997. Thereafter the forum will meet at least every six months but initially may meet quarterly.

The idea for the forum came from a paper published in March 1995 by the British Shippers Council entitled Air Freight - the shipper's needs. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
